title: Sybil: Deep Learning Predicts 1–6 Year Lung Cancer Risk From a Single Chest CT
whyItMatters: Forecasts an individual’s risk of developing lung cancer up to 6 years in advance from a single low-dose chest CT scan—with no clinical metadata—achieving 0.86–0.94 1-year AUC across US and Taiwanese cohorts.
summary: Developed by Peter Mikhael, Jeremy Wohlwend, Lecia Sequist, Regina Barzilay, and colleagues at MIT and Massachusetts General Hospital, Sybil (Journal of Clinical Oncology, 2023) is an open-source 3D deep learning model that analyzes raw low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) lung volumes alone—without radiologist annotations or smoking history—to predict future lung cancer incidence over 1 to 6 years. Across three independent validation sets (NLST, MGH, and Chang Gung Memorial Hospital in Taiwan, including never-smokers), Sybil achieved 1-year AUCs of 0.86–0.94 and 6-year AUCs of 0.75–0.81, identifying subtle pre-diagnostic imaging signatures invisible to the human eye.
technicalHighlights: Achieved 1-year ROC-AUC of 0.92 on NLST, 0.86 on MGH, and 0.94 on Chang Gung Memorial Hospital (Taiwan), maintaining 0.75–0.81 AUC six years out.
Requires only a single raw LDCT volume with zero clinical variables, demographic inputs, or radiologist bounding boxes at inference.
Generalized across an external Taiwanese cohort containing a high proportion of never-smokers ineligible under traditional US screening guidelines.
caveats: Retrospective validation cohorts under-represented Black and Hispanic populations, and prospective clinical trials are ongoing to determine optimal follow-up screening intervals without causing overdiagnosis.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated that deep 3D vision models can detect sub-clinical oncogenic risk signals years before visible tumors form.
scoreRationale.ripple: Opened personalized risk-adapted cancer screening for both smokers and high-risk never-smokers worldwide.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in the Journal of Clinical Oncology with multi-continent external validation and open-source weights.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compresses 6-year longitudinal risk stratification into real-time inference from one standard screening CT.
